# x-mutti reference

<!-- Generated by `make docs` from internal/project. Do not edit. -->

mutti's settings in a Compose file. Every key is optional.

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | The project's name, part of every hostname. Default: the main worktree's directory name. |
| `main` | string | The service behind the instance's main hostname. Default: the service publishing or exposing the most typical web port (80, 3000, 4200, 5173, 8000, 8080). |
| `routes` | map of object | HTTP routes per service. Default: the main service on the main hostname, every other service publishing or exposing an HTTP port on <service>.<main hostname>. |
| `routes.<name>.host` | string | Subdomain under the main hostname; "" is the main hostname itself. Default: the service name, or "" for the main service. |
| `routes.<name>.path` | string | Path prefix on the main hostname that also leads to the service, e.g. /api. |
| `routes.<name>.port` | integer | Container port to send traffic to. Default: the service's first published TCP port, else its first exposed one. |
| `ports` | map of list of integer | Container ports to publish on a fixed host port, per service, for tools that keep a connection setting, such as database GUIs. The port follows from instance, service and port, so it stays the same across restarts. |
| `worktree` | object | Settings for mutti worktree add. |
| `worktree.copy` | list of string | Files and directories (globs allowed) that git does not track but a worktree needs, such as .env.local; copied from the main worktree into new ones, never overwriting. |
| `exec` | object | How mutti exec, mutti shell and hooks run commands. |
| `exec.user` | string | "host" (default): the host user's uid:gid, so files in bind mounts belong to you; "service": the image's user; or an explicit user[:group]. |
| `exec.home` | string | $HOME for commands run as the host user, who has no home in the image. Default /tmp. |
| `hooks` | object | Commands run inside services at points of an instance's life. |
| `hooks.bootstrap` | list of object | Once per instance, after its first successful up. |
| `hooks.bootstrap[].service` | string | Service to run the command in; it must be running. |
| `hooks.bootstrap[].run` | string | Shell command, run with sh -c inside the service. |
| `hooks.bootstrap[].user` | string | Like exec.user; empty means exec.user. |
| `hooks.post-up` | list of object | After every up. |
| `hooks.post-up[].service` | string | Service to run the command in; it must be running. |
| `hooks.post-up[].run` | string | Shell command, run with sh -c inside the service. |
| `hooks.post-up[].user` | string | Like exec.user; empty means exec.user. |
| `hooks.pre-down` | list of object | Before down, destroy and reset; a failure is reported but does not stop the teardown. |
| `hooks.pre-down[].service` | string | Service to run the command in; it must be running. |
| `hooks.pre-down[].run` | string | Shell command, run with sh -c inside the service. |
| `hooks.pre-down[].user` | string | Like exec.user; empty means exec.user. |
| `hooks.after-clone` | list of object | Instead of bootstrap when the data was copied from another instance (worktree add --data-from): the data needs no setup, the worktree may. |
| `hooks.after-clone[].service` | string | Service to run the command in; it must be running. |
| `hooks.after-clone[].run` | string | Shell command, run with sh -c inside the service. |
| `hooks.after-clone[].user` | string | Like exec.user; empty means exec.user. |
| `hooks.sweep` | list of object | On mutti sweep, with MUTTI_SWEEP_OLDER_THAN in seconds: remove per-run resources the project made inside services, such as test databases named after run ids. |
| `hooks.sweep[].service` | string | Service to run the command in; it must be running. |
| `hooks.sweep[].run` | string | Shell command, run with sh -c inside the service. |
| `hooks.sweep[].user` | string | Like exec.user; empty means exec.user. |
| `overlays` | map of list of string | Named sets of extra Compose files, enabled with --overlay <name>. Without --overlay, commands other than up and run use the overlays the instance was last started with. |
